steps: Boil the baby potatoes for about 12 minutes until almost soft, then drain.
Peel them once cool enough to hold and prick each one all over with a fork.
Blend the onion, ginger and garlic to a smooth paste, then blend in the curd for a few seconds.
Heat the ghee, add the bay leaf, then add the paste and cook on low, stirring, until it thickens and the ghee shows, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, sugar, salt and green chilli.
Add the potatoes with a little water to make a thick gravy.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes.
Crush in the kasuri methi, add the coriander leaves and let it rest 5 minutes before serving.
note: One source used about 60 g of potatoes a person and two used 125 g; this goes with 125 g, a fair share when dum aloo is the main dish. Tomato was left out because two of the three recipes use none.
